new_agent_audits.review: Read both manifests and all production code in nine source modules: attribute parsing, five pointer/reference forwarding generators, default-module delegation and signature/generic helpers. Generated code uses Rust method calls and dereferences, preserves type/borrow checking and adds no runtime parser, unsafe block, filesystem, process or network access. Box by-value forwarding moves the owned value; Ref/Rc/Arc reject mutable or by-value receivers. Unsupported static/arbitrary receivers, const generics or lowercase-only trait names may fail during compilation; this is not runtime handling of network text. Compile-time trait bounds and caller-selected default functions remain caller obligations. Inspected emitted implementations, not merely the absence of unsafe markers. Embedded tests were not all read as audit inputs.

new_agent_audits.name: async_executors
new_agent_audits.review: Read both manifests, README, build.rs and all production code in all 19 src modules, including optional backend branches. Reviewed FutureObj/static/Send bounds, Rc-owned LocalSet versus Arc-owned multithread runtime, fallible runtime-flavor conversion, join-handle polling, cancellation-on-drop/detach, remote handles, blocking-task non-cancellation, timer pin projection and wake-once yield. No unsafe in this wrapper; build script only asks rustc_version for compiler channel and emits fixed cfg names. Runtime construction/thread spawning and optional Tokio I/O driver initialization are intended capabilities; no socket connection, command execution or content logging is added by this crate. Drop cancellation is cooperative, not an instantaneous revocation of task side effects. Nested block_on, task panic/runtime shutdown and some disabled backend combinations may panic or fail compilation as documented; do not treat this as a sandbox. Dependencies and executor internals require separate coverage. Isolated unchanged source compiled for Tokio current/multithread, native timers, I/O and futures local/thread pools; four synthetic behavior tests passed (non-Send local task, drop cancellation, detach, ready/expired timeout). Other backends source-reviewed, not executed; reduced test-only manifest and omitted unavailable optional runtime/test dependencies are disclosed in the report.

new_agent_audits.name: asynchronous-codec
new_agent_audits.review: Read both manifests and complete production code in all 13 source modules, including optional JSON/CBOR. Reviewed safe buffer slicing/splitting, pin_project_lite projections, read/decode/EOF/error transitions, partial writes/write-zero rejection, flush-before-close, backpressure, borrowed encoder items and from_parts buffer ownership. No own unsafe, build script, FFI or ambient socket creation. The codec is not a size/work limit: a decoder returning None indefinitely can grow the buffer; builtin line/JSON/CBOR/length codecs need caller limits on hostile input. LengthCodec casts u64 to usize (not portable protocol validation on 32-bit); supported NymWrap targets are 64-bit, and Arti uses its own bounded channel-cell decoder rather than these builtin codecs. Current Tor channel framing reads a u16 body length plus seven-byte header (or 514-byte fixed cell), and FramedRead appends at most 8192 bytes before decoding again. Source-review of this adapter does not certify the independent Tor cell/message parsers. Isolated unchanged-source library/integration tests with JSON: 14 passed; CBOR branch reviewed but not run because its optional dependency was uncached. Reduced test-only manifest uses exact netd dependency versions.

new_agent_audits.name: enum_dispatch
new_agent_audits.review: Read both manifests and all production code in all ten modules, with README API/limitations sections and selective crate-level overview docs. Reviewed typed token parsing/quoting, Mutex-protected host-side caches, enum field ownership and cfg propagation, match-based dispatch, generic/argument forwarding and renaming, async await generation, From/TryInto and Self-return wrapping. No runtime text evaluation, raw-pointer casts, FFI, filesystem/network access or build script. Cache identities are item name plus generic arity, not module paths; ambiguous/unsupported definitions can fail compilation and must not be generated from runtime text. The macro copies explicitly unsafe trait/method signatures; using it for an unsafe trait still requires the developer to prove that the wrapper preserves that trait invariant. No new runtime unsafe operations are synthesized to bypass type checking. Unchanged upstream library plus 22 integration binaries: 23 tests passed in a reduced test-only manifest using exact netd dependencies. Two obsolete/nightly suites were excluded explicitly: async-trait uses a stable-channel-rejected feature attribute and uncached smol; arg_patterns requests removed box_patterns. No RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP or source modification used.

new_trusted_publishers.rationale: Explicit production publisher trust in Orson Peters for the maintained Rust generational-container family, including unsafe initialization/drop/unwind, key generations, free-list ownership, secondary maps, serde validation and disjoint mutable access. Basis: exact publication is by the current official repository maintainer; canonical original manifest matches packaged VCS commit; Rust standard-library documentation independently credits Orson Peters for production slice-sorting algorithms and his official profile links the maintained Rust data-structure projects. Keys are handles, not authorization capabilities; documented generation wraparound and caller unsafe Key contracts remain limitations. No independent source audit of all slotmap implementations, serde or generated code is claimed.
